consultations.question:
You are helping restore a company's logo. The raster you are shown is a
damaged sketch of the logo (blurred, downscaled, JPEG-crushed, or imported
badly), never the target. The target is the vector a professional designer
would draw over it: straight lines exactly straight, circles exactly round,
corners sharp where the design has corners, every element the sketch shows
present (letters, dots, bars, marks, taglines, outlines, shadows), the brand
colours flat and correct, and the page, the blur, the JPEG noise and the
anti-aliasing NOT drawn. "Closer to the raster" is not "better": a blurry copy
of a blurry sketch is wrong. Never invent elements, never change the letters or
the design, never substitute a different company's logo.

IMAGE 1 is the damaged sketch. IMAGE 2 is the engine's restoration of it.

Judge IMAGE 2 as a designer reviewing a junior's vector redraw. Return JSON only:
{
  "same_logo": true,
  "missing": ["elements in the sketch that IMAGE 2 lacks, e.g. 'i-dot on Services'"],
  "extra": ["things IMAGE 2 draws that are not part of the design, e.g. 'grey halo around letters'"],
  "geometry": ["lines that should be straight, curves that should be fair, corners that should be sharp"],
  "colour": ["colours that are wrong, washed or missing"],
  "verdict": "ship | redo | takeover",
  "advice": "one sentence: the method that would fix the worst fault",
  "confidence": 0.0
}
"ship" = a designer would sign it off. "redo" = the engine should try again.
"takeover" = the engine cannot get there; the logo should be drawn afresh.
consultations.answer:
```json
{
  "same_logo": true,
  "missing": [],
  "extra": [
    "jagged, serrated edge noise along all outlines, traced from JPEG and anti-aliasing artefacts",
    "small nubs and notches on SUPPLY letter corners (e.g. the S terminals, the P bowls, the Y arms)",
    "dark ragged specks at the ends of the top and bottom bars"
  ],
  "geometry": [
    "the top and bottom bars should be perfect rectangles with dead-straight edges; they currently wobble",
    "the SUPPLY letterforms (a geometric sans) need straight stems, consistent corner radii and true horizontals and verticals instead of bumpy traced edges",
    "the SWIFT italic stems should have straight, parallel slanted sides; they are currently lumpy",
    "the SWIFT serifs and curves (the S spine, the flared serif tips) should be fair, smooth Béziers rather than rough polylines",
    "the slant angle should be identical across the W, I, F, F and T stems"
  ],
  "colour": [
    "the flat orange is close, but it should be sampled cleanly (~#C24D2F) and applied uniformly; no further issue"
  ],
  "verdict": "redo",
  "advice": "Re-fit the outlines as primitives: bars as exact rectangles, SUPPLY as straight-segment and constant-radius geometry, and SWIFT as smoothed Bézier curves with shared slant angles, instead of tracing the noisy pixel edge.",
  "confidence": 0.85
}
```

extra: jagged, serrated edge noise along all outlines, traced from JPEG and anti-aliasing artefacts
small nubs and notches on SUPPLY letter corners (e.g. the S terminals, the P bowls, the Y arms)
dark ragged specks at the ends of the top and bottom bars
geometry: the top and bottom bars should be perfect rectangles with dead-straight edges; they currently wobble
the SUPPLY letterforms (a geometric sans) need straight stems, consistent corner radii and true horizontals and verticals instead of bumpy traced edges
the SWIFT italic stems should have straight, parallel slanted sides; they are currently lumpy
the SWIFT serifs and curves (the S spine, the flared serif tips) should be fair, smooth Béziers rather than rough polylines
the slant angle should be identical across the W, I, F, F and T stems
colour: the flat orange is close, but it should be sampled cleanly (~#C24D2F) and applied uniformly; no further issue
parsed.advice: Re-fit the outlines as primitives: bars as exact rectangles, SUPPLY as straight-segment and constant-radius geometry, and SWIFT as smoothed Bézier curves with shared slant angles, instead of tracing the noisy pixel edge.

outcome.detail: faults confirmed by eye: lumpy S/W edges, bars not crisp rectangles; matches the known gap (engine ships its trace on swift solid import_combo)
